It is possible. Try to create a backup on an external hard drive first. Make sure you have the new laptop drivers on cd, if you don't have the driver cd then go download them all from the website. You absolutely must have the drivers for the new motherboard, chipset, proc, audio, video, usb, ethernet, wifi, touchpad, for this to work.

To move windows to a different model laptop you first need to change the video drivers. Uninstall the video drivers, and change it to generic VGA. Reboot to make sure it works. Uninstall any drivers for hardware you know is changing like touchpad, audio, wifi, ethernet. Then move the drive over and try to boot to F8 safe mode. If that works reboot and then check device manager for conflicts, uninstall the drivers with problems. Then reboot and start installing your new laptop drivers.

If it hangs and won't load into safe\normal mode, you might need to run the windows installer over the top. (to redetect and reinstall the correct motherboard\chipset drivers).

It is highly doubtful you'll be successful at migrating the OS to a new system for a variety of reasons. Microsoft used to (and probably still does) tie a Windows license to a particular system, which it recognizes by scanning the components when the OS is installed. Move the OS to a new system and they'll think you're running a pirated version. This has caused headaches for people upgrading their rigs because too much new hardware is interpreted as a different computer which then gets labelled as pirated.

On top of that, your system is a Dell and the OEM install is probably even more rigorously tied to the system.

As others have noted, and as you probably have already done, your best bet is to backup your drive and just move on to a new system. If it is merely your battery failing, you shouldn't have problems if the laptop is plugged in and getting power directly from the charger. If you still have problems when your computer is plugged in, then it probably ain't the battery.

Probably isn't what you want to hear, but working on laptops is always a PITA anyway. It's extremely difficult to upgrade them or move components around, so when they start having problems you pretty much have to trash them and get something new.
